# FG-REPO-0020

| 項目 | 値 |
|---|---|
| HTTP ステータス | 500 |
| 重大度 | alert |
| Runbook | [`repository-purge`](../../ops/runbooks/repository-purge.md) |
| 発生させるテスト | `a_failed_purge_is_repository_purge_stuck_and_retried_next_run` |

## 利用者向けメッセージ

- ja: 削除したプロジェクトの完全削除が終わっていません。問い合わせ番号を添えて管理者に連絡してください。
- en: The purge of a deleted project has not finished. Contact the administrator with the request ID.
- id: Penghapusan permanen proyek yang dihapus belum selesai. Hubungi administrator dengan menyertakan ID permintaan.

## 原因 (cause)

The purge (step D5 MR4, ADR-0015 Amendment D5: the `purge` task of `forge worker` every `hosting.purge_interval_secs`, or `forge admin project purge --now`) could not finish one project whose grace period is over. The purge has two phases: (1) one transaction moves the repository to `purging` (after that the project can no longer be restored, FG-REPO-0019 reason=purging); (2) the bare directory is removed from the storage root (renamed aside, then deleted, bounded by a deadline) and one transaction deletes the rows (members, protected refs, repository, namespace, project), writes the `deleted` tombstone of the path, the `project.purged` audit row and event. A failure in either phase leaves the project as it was at the end of the last completed step; the next run resumes it (a `purging` repository never goes back to `ready`). `step` says where it failed: `lock` (taking the project's purge lock: the database), `start` (phase 1: the database), `provision_check` (reading the state of the repository's provisioning job), `storage` (the directory: FG-REPO-0001 a symlink or a file where the repository or a leftover should be — possible tampering, FG-REPO-0003 an I/O failure), `finish` (phase 2's transaction). Not failures (no code): a project whose purge lock another purge holds, and a removal slower than the run's 120 s wait (it goes on in the background holding the lock) — both are `forge.repo.purge_deferred` (`reason=in_progress` / `removal_running`).

## 調べ方 (diagnosis)

The log event of the purge task (`task=purge`, or the CLI's) carries `step`, `project_id`, `repo_id`, `cause_code` (the code of the underlying failure, whose own `context` is in `source`) and `overdue_s` (seconds since `purge_after`). The same project failing on every run is stuck; one failure followed by `forge.repo.purged` for that project was transient. Look at the state with privileged queries: SELECT state FROM forge.repositories WHERE project_id = <id>; SELECT deleted_at, purge_after FROM forge.projects WHERE id = <id>. `forge admin repo-path <repo_id>` prints the directory and whether it still exists; leftovers of an interrupted removal are named `.purge-<repo_id>-*.git` (and of an interrupted provisioning `.tmp-<repo_id>-*.git`) in the same shard directory. `cause_code=FG-DB-0009 reason=rejected` in `start` means the database guard refused `purging` (the project is not pending deletion or its grace period is not over: a clock difference, or a restore committed in between — it is skipped on the next run). A purge also waits (`forge.repo.purge_deferred`, not an error) while the repository's provisioning job is running.

## 対処 (fix)

Follow the runbook: for FG-REPO-0003 free space or fix the permissions of the storage root, for FG-REPO-0001 inspect what is at the path (never delete it blindly: a symlink there may point outside the storage root), for database failures restore database access. Then run `forge admin project purge --dry-run` to see what is due and `forge admin project purge --now` (an approved runbook step) or wait for the next run of the worker: the purge resumes where it stopped and is idempotent (a directory already gone is not an error, the rows and the event are written once).
